issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, coolant drips at the front of the engine, overheating, or milky oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The intake manifold gaskets break down where coolant passes through them and begin leaking, either outside the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Do not keep driving with a falling coolant level or milky oil. Have the gaskets replaced and the oil checked for coolant before the bearings are damaged.

issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or late shifts, starting off in second gear, dropping out of fourth, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: The 4T65-E four-speed automatic in these cars is known for internal wear, including a worn pressure valve bore in the channel plate that starves the shift solenoids of pressure.
issues.next: Have the transmission checked at the first sign of slipping rather than driving until it quits, and keep the fluid fresh.

issues.t: No reverse or slipping in reverse when warm
issues.sym: Reverse engages slowly, slips, or does not engage at all once the car is warmed up; a fluid leak may show at the reverse servo cover.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for reverse slipping when hot and for fluid leaking past the reverse servo cover on this transmission.
issues.next: Have a shop check the bulletins against your VIN. Avoid relying on reverse in tight spots until it is fixed.

issues.sym: A shudder or vibration as the transmission shifts from first to second.
issues.why: GM traced this to the second clutch assembly in the transmission and issued a repair bulletin.
issues.next: Have a transmission shop check for the bulletin; the fix replaces the second clutch parts.

issues.sym: A window grinds, clicks, stops partway, or drops down into the door.
issues.why: The window regulators in this generation wear out and break.
issues.next: Replace the regulator. Tape or wedge the window closed in the meantime to keep weather out.

issues.t: Oil leaking onto the exhaust manifold can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell or smoke from the engine bay, especially after hard braking.
issues.why: The front valve cover gasket runs hot and can seep oil onto the exhaust manifold, where it can ignite. GM recalled 1997-2003 supercharged cars and later added early 2004 cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, stop and have it checked before driving further, and do not park it in a garage until it is repaired.

issues.sym: The key will not turn to the lock position or will not come out after parking.
issues.why: The column thinks the car is not in park, usually because of the shifter not seating fully in park, its park-lock cable or wiring, or a worn lock cylinder.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in park. Have the shifter cable, park-lock switch and lock cylinder checked rather than leaving the key in.

issues.t: Ignition switch can turn off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off unexpectedly, especially with a heavy key ring or over bumps, and power steering and brake assist are lost.
issues.why: The ignition switch could slip out of Run, which can also keep the airbags from deploying. GM recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and carry only the ignition key until it is done.

issues.sym: The ABS light comes on now and then or stays on.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for intermittent or constant ABS warning lights on these cars; wheel speed sensor wiring and hubs are frequent causes.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking still works, but the anti-lock function may be off until it is fixed.

issues.t: Headlights and daytime lights may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The headlamps or daytime running lights do not come on.
issues.why: The headlamp driver module can overheat and fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the module replaced. Do not drive at night without working headlights.
